finding.claim: The purge handler checks the admin permission but discards the result, so any caller can invoke the destructive purgeAll operation.
finding.source: Any HTTP request that reaches the purge route with a user in context, including users without the admin permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 (protected admin-only destructive operation)

trace.note: checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is discarded, so nothing is enforced

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) computes the permission but its result is unused. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is the enforcing helper and is not called in purge. rotateKeys (handlers.go:31-38) correctly calls mustPerm and returns early, so purge is the inconsistent handler. No middleware in this repo enforces admin on the route. purgeAll and rotateAll are empty stubs (handlers.go:44-45), so impact is nil in this snapshot and becomes critical once purgeAll does real work.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool that is discarded as a bare statement at handlers.go:26. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is never called in purge. The only enforcing check in this snapshot is in rotateKeys (handlers.go:33). No route registration or middleware in this directory enforces admin on the purge path (Grep found no HandleFunc/Handle registration).
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any request that has a user in context (userFrom at handlers.go:25 panics otherwise), with no enforcing guard before it. Caveat: route registration is not in this snapshot, so the reachable-role claim rests on the handler code alone, and impact is nil while purgeAll is an empty stub (handlers.go:44).

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked type assertion, so a request reaching a handler without a stored *User panics, and handlers that rely on it dereference a nil user.
finding.source: A request that reaches a handler without auth middleware having stored a *User under userKey{} (depends on route registration, which is not in this repo).
finding.sink: Unchecked .(*User) assertion at handlers.go:40, followed by u.Perms access in checkPerm/mustPerm (handlers.go:13, :17)

trace.note: Unchecked type assertion panics if the context value is missing or of the wrong type

finding.guards_checked: None in this file. net/http recovers panics per connection, so impact is request failure, not process crash. This is only a fail-open risk if a route is registered without auth; route registration is not in the repo, so this is low confidence and needs confirmation.

verdict.guard_found: Per-request recovery from net/http (stdlib, not in repo). The panic at handlers.go:40 fires before any effect: purgeAll() at :27 and rotateAll() at :36 are never reached, so the failure is fail-closed. Separately, checkPerm at :26 returns a bool that is discarded, which is a real missing admin check in purge, but that is a different finding from this one.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (userFrom at handlers.go:25, :32, and the unchecked assertion at :40), but a missing user makes the handler panic at :40 before purgeAll (:27) or rotateAll (:36) runs, so it fails closed and yields only a failed request, not a fail-open security issue. The real problem in this file is that purge discards the checkPerm result at handlers.go:26, which should be reported as its own finding.
